newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-CHAMPIONS DORTMUND BEAT ST PAULI, GO FIFTH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHAMPIONS DORTMUND BEAT ST PAULI, GO FIFTH.

text.p: German champions Borussia Dortmund beat St Pauli 2-1 in a stormy encounter which saw three sendings-off on Sunday to go fifth in the first division.
St Pauli's Tore Pedersen set the tone in the 12th minute when he was dismissed for a reckless tackle from behind on striker Heiko Herrlich.
But even against 10 men, Dortmund struggled until playmaker Andy Moeller curled a trademark free-kick over St Pauli's wall in the 36th minute to give the champions the lead.
Captain Michael Zorc was dismissed for a second yellow-card offence just before halftime, but Dortmund's pressure paid off when Juergen Kohler tapped in a Stefan Reuter cross in the 52nd minute.

Andre Trulsen pulled one back for the visiting side in the 74th minute, slotting home a ball which had ricocheted back to him off Herrlich. But there was more trouble for St Pauli when Brazilian striker Luiz Emerson was sent off for punching Kohler.
The win took Dortmund to 16 points, three behind leaders VfB Stuttgart, and left St Pauli marooned one from bottom.
